title: Circular storm-flattened spots in wheat (letter)
claim: Flattened circular spots caused by 'cyclonic wind action'
reception: First scientific description of the phenomenon

title: The formation of circular-symmetric crop-damage patterns by atmospheric vortices
claim: Circles made by electrically charged spinning air masses ('plasma vortices')
reception: Collapsed after 1991 confession & complex pictograms; Zuckerman criticized methodology

title: The Circles Effect and Its Mysteries (book)
The Crop-Circle Phenomenon: An Investigative Report
claim: Frequency escalation, geographic clustering, complexity evolution and 'shyness effect' all indicate hoaxing/social contagion
reception: Seminal skeptical analysis; used Delgado & Andrews' own data

title: Crop circle geometry & diatonic ratios
claim: Formations embed Euclidean theorems and musical (diatonic) ratios
reception: Hawkins himself concluded human creators with advanced mathematical ability

title: Anatomical anomalies in crop formation plants
claim: Node swelling, expulsion cavities and germination changes 'cannot be accounted for by hoaxes'; transient heating implied
reception: Criticized (Nickell 1996; Grassi et al. 2005): no blinding, mundane causes not excluded; never independently replicated

title: Semi-Molten Meteoric Iron Associated with a Crop Formation
claim: Iron 'glaze' of fused meteoritic particles in a Cherhill 1993 formation
reception: Circlemaker Rob Irving says he dumped iron filings there as an art action — a cautionary tale

title: Crop-Circle Mania: An Investigative Update
claim: Secret 'shoelace' marker planted in a man-made circle; cereologists endorsed the circle as genuine

title: Dispersion of energies in worldwide crop formations
claim: Node-length gradients fit EM energy absorption; >95% of formations attributed to ion plasma vortices
reception: Main target of Grassi et al. 2005 statistical critique

title: Opinions and comments on Levengood & Talbott (1999)
claim: Node-lengthening in two Dutch circles fits a point EM source ('ball of light') ~4.1 m above the field
reception: Rebutted by Grassi et al. (2005); Haselhoff replied in JSE 2007

title: The Deepening Complexity of Crop Circles (book)
claim: Scientific case for anomalous circle origin

title: Circular Reasoning: The 'Mystery' of Crop Circles and Their 'Orbs' of Light
claim: Orb/light reports consistent with mundane causes; patterns traceable to human makers

authors: F. Grassi, C. Cocheo & P. Russo
title: Balls of Light: The Questionable Science of Crop Circles
claim: Physiologia Plantarum crop-circle papers are pseudoscientific: sample sizes unstated, data selection, heating cannot explain nodes
reception: Physiologia Plantarum refused to publish it; JSE exchange continued 2007

title: Spatial distribution of England's crop circles: Using GIS to investigate a geo-spatial mystery
claim: 2002 English formations: 46% Wiltshire; ~44% within 15 km of Avebury; 32% within 3 km of trunk roads
reception: Key statistical-geography paper: distribution indicates human agency

title: Playing Puck (MPhil thesis)
claim: Circle-making as performative art; documents the iron-filings episode

title: Crop circle tales: narrative testimonies from the Dutch Frontier Science Movement
claim: Crop-circle lore as Dutch frontier-science subculture narrative

title: The crop circle evolves
claim: Crop circles as a growing underground art movement blending math & technology
reception: Widely cited mainstream framing as art

title: Coming soon to a field near you: the physics of crop-circle formation
claim: Modern makers could use GPS, lasers and microwave magnetrons to reproduce node anomalies (he replicated them himself)
reception: Major press coverage ('GPS, lasers and microwaves')

authors: E.H. Haselhoff, A. Boerman & R. Bobbink
title: An experimental study for reproduction of biological anomalies (Hoeven 1999)
claim: Attempts to reproduce node anomalies experimentally
